I therefore prioritize matched intermediate points and loading contrasts, while retaining ordinary anchors so retraining does not convert tail-repair labels into a global broadening.","batch_rationale":"The batch combines local response curves for m45, m107, m208, m66, m146, m212, m211, m216, and m72 with loading contrasts for m80, m51, m60, m128, and m89. These experiments target the observed failure regions while testing whether the failures are caused by solvent strength, loading, or chemical family. Five molecule-novel rows broaden chemical coverage across halogenated, amino, aldehyde, and ester neighborhoods. The final anchor group samples narrow ordinary predictions across simple aromatic, ester, hydrocarbon, and oxygenated families. Together, the batch should improve generalization by teaching both the boundaries of late-tail regimes and the ordinary rows that dominate the Row-distribution."}
